metadata.description: The syslog dialect of log shipping: the elements RFC 9742 (the IETF syslog management model) gives a remote destination, which every syslog sender already speaks — rsyslog and syslog-ng on hosts, Redfish EventDestination on BMCs, OpenConfig system-logging on switches. Adds transport, message format and the facility filter. Named for the protocol, which is a standard, never for a sender.

source.description: Which logs: the systemd journal (default), on-disk files, the device's own log (`native`, for appliances, BMCs and switches that send their own syslog), container logs, or audit logs.

min_severity.description: Ship messages at this severity and above, named as in RFC 5424 and compared as in RFC 9742 ("equals-or-higher"). OpenTelemetry maps the same names onto its severity numbers, so the filter means the same thing on either protocol. Absent ships everything.

labels.description: Extra resource attributes stamped on every message, named per the OpenTelemetry semantic conventions (`deployment.environment`, `service.name`). The provider always stamps the target's `host.name` and `udlm.handle` itself, so a log line can be followed back to its record.

transport.description: How messages travel. `udp` (RFC 5426) and `tls` (RFC 5425) are the two RFC 9742 names; `tcp` (RFC 6587 framing) and `relp` are the further values Redfish EventDestination offers. Prefer `tls`: it is the only one that is both reliable and private.

format.description: Message format. `rfc5424` (default) carries structured data and a full timestamp; `rfc3164` is the legacy BSD format some devices still send.

facilities.description: Ship only these facilities, named as the RFC 9742 facility identities. Absent ships every facility. Combined with `min_severity`, this is the RFC 9742 selector.

status.description: Realized health of the shipper (e.g. running / degraded), as reported by discovery.

shipping_to.description: The intake endpoint the shipper is delivering to, resolved from the store's published intake (echo of realized config).

last_shipped_at.description: OBSERVED — a provider-watched liveness fact, not derivable from model records (no shipment-instance records exist; this is heartbeat, not history). Timestamp of the most recent message the store received from this target (RFC 3339) — drives staleness detection.

relationships.name: sink
relationships.description: The log store the logs go to. The shipper binds the store's published `intake_endpoints` output that matches its protocol, so moving the store's receiver changes one record, not every shipper.

relationships.name: host
relationships.description: The machine whose logs are shipped (a VM or a bare-metal host). Exactly one of host, bmc, switch, gateway or cluster is set.

relationships.name: bmc
relationships.description: The baseboard management controller whose own log is shipped (`source` native).

relationships.name: switch
relationships.description: The switch whose own log is shipped (`source` native).

relationships.name: gateway
relationships.description: The gateway whose own log is shipped (`source` native).

relationships.name: cluster
relationships.description: The cluster whose container, node or audit logs are shipped by a cluster-level forwarder.

adopts.role: the attribute names in `labels` and the identity the provider stamps (`host.name`)

context.purpose: Ships a resource's logs over syslog.
context.plain_description: A LogShipper that speaks syslog: which transport (TLS preferred), which message format, and which facilities to send. These are the settings RFC 9742 defines for a remote syslog destination, so a host agent, a BMC and a switch all read the same record the same way. The destination address is not here; it comes from the LogStore's published syslog intake.
use_when: The sender speaks syslog — a host agent, an appliance, a BMC or a switch.
works_with: LogStore — whose `intake` must offer `syslog` over the same transport.
